differentiators.observation: Transactional one-off scheduling — the exact capability the frozen LLP 0121 verdict named as why a builder 'would still choose Convex for the Dispatch workload' — now works on the public packaged closure as an external consumer: ctx.jobs.enqueue rides the SAME serialized transaction as the producing write (a rejected create schedules nothing), the confirmed mutation envelope carries bounded enqueues facts ({jobId, action, availableAtMs} — never argument values), the job row carries producer association (producerMutationId), and the injected-clock drain makes every schedule fact collectable deterministically. Convex's ctx.scheduler.runAfter offers the one-call ergonomics but no receipt-level producer association and no deterministic drain seam.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: Enqueue atomicity with the producing transaction; bounded enqueues facts on confirmed receipts and their absence on rejections; idempotencyKey custody (REUSED/RACED codes); the injected-clock forced drain.

differentiators.observation: Zero-ceremony contention-safe sequence allocation: six concurrent creates from two clients allocated JOB-4..JOB-9 dense and duplicate-free with a three-line counter read-increment-write, because serialized mutation commits make it correct — the exact capability the frozen Convex chat evidence flags as missing ('compare-and-swap on server sequences', Diary 0028; 'would need a contention-safe sequence allocation', Diary 0034; LLP 0125's improvement row). The dedupe replay returned the committed job without burning the counter.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: Serialized commit order making read-increment-write collision-free; unique-index-backed dedupe replay returning the committed row.

differentiators.observation: Ownership fencing with an auditable ledger as plain app logic: concurrent claims resolve to one owner, the loser learns the authoritative owner, and a PRIOR owner's stale-fence writes leave append-only fenced receipts (byte-stable prefixes across three snapshots) — evidence-grade custody that frozen SpacetimeDB evidence delivers only as intentional reducer rejections (refusal without a receipt ledger) and frozen Convex arms hand-rolled without receipts.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: In-transaction ownership + fence checks writing only receipts on the late path; append-only attempt ledgers surviving as authoritative history.

differentiators.observation: Idempotent external dispatch with provider-boundary proof: across a same-actor retry AND a two-actor concurrent race the strict external provider received exactly ONE request per dedupe key (streamAttempt custody; the loser observed 'deduped'), settlement landed as one inspectable ledger row, and the canary secret reached the provider while staying absent from every client-visible surface — where the frozen Convex research-room arm carries its Stop-class argv/wildcard secret defect.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: streamAttempt terminal-winner custody keyed by the app dedupe key; ctx.secrets staging with value-free diagnostics; unique-index settlement dedupe.

differentiators.observation: Operational evidence velocity: the full 10-check suite — fresh versioned-seed install, ten sign-ins, concurrency barriers, cron ticks with a real maintenance sweep, an injected-clock one-off drain, external dispatch with a strict provider, export/reset/restore with digest proof, and two receipted reset-installs — runs in 5.0s wall. The deterministic tick seam, the forced drain, and the receipted reset-install are what make an OPERATIONS contract testable without sleeping on cadences.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: Machine-readable dev lifecycle; admin tick seam; injected-clock jobs drain; receipted reset-install restoring the literal fixture including named-empty runtime tables.

differentiators.observation: App-level export/restore round-trips through a receipted destructive reset with DIGEST equality over an id-free natural-key projection (jobs by seq, children by (jobSeq, seq), receipts by dedupeKey), and the restore is itself an audited ledger event — no frozen competitor arm demonstrated an application-authored restore with byte-level proof.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: Receipted reset-install semantics (resetDeletedRows, expectedDataVersionStream fencing); serialized restore mutations making upsert-by-natural-key correct.
